statements.proposition: This change keeps the existing interfaces of the connection classes and connection manager working as before (backward compatible) throughout the codebase.
statements.label: FALSE
statements.note: Calling convention broken between ConnectionManager and every connection class. At base, ConnectionManager.perform_action calls connection.perform_action(action_name, kwargs) with kwargs as a positional dict, and connections (e.g. twitter, solana) defined perform_action(self, action_name, kwargs). At head the connection manager line is unchanged, but all 19 connection classes now define perform_action(self, action_name, **kwargs) and accept no second positional argument, so the call raises TypeError (caught and logged by the manager, returning None). Established by reading source at base and head; not executed (static Python call semantics). Other incompatibilities exist (config becomes a Pydantic object, so self.config['x'] dict access no longer works) but the perform_action break alone settles it.
evidence: head src/connection_manager.py line 215: `return connection.perform_action(action_name, kwargs)` (unchanged from base line 207)
base src/connections/twitter_connection.py:347 and solana_connection.py:418: `def perform_action(self, action_name: str, kwargs)`
head: `grep -n 'def perform_action' src/connections/*.py` shows all 19 classes as `(self, action_name: str, **kwargs)` e.g. openai_connection.py:191
OpenAIConnection base used self.config['model']; head uses cast(OpenAIConfig, self.config).model (config is now a Pydantic model)
